title: Benchmarking of geometric accuracy in PBF-LB/M: approach to expand VDI 3405 for AlSi10Mg (Krasniqi et al., euspen SIG Advancing Precision in Additive Manufacturing, Berlin, October 2025)
publisher: euspen; authors at Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt and Bundesanstalt fuer Materialforschung und -pruefung

rights.attribution: M. Krasniqi, K. Poka, R. Laquai, S. Ali, A. Ulbricht, W. Brandes, U. Neuschaefer-Rube, M. Epperlein, F. Loeffler, K. Hilgenberg

notes: Four-page conference paper downloaded and read as text on 2026-11-12; the figures were not read. A compact AlSi10Mg test artefact was built on an EOS M 300-4 (60 micrometre layers, beam diameter about 84 micrometres, beam offset 0.2 mm, powder d10/d50/d90 25/44/73 micrometres) and on a DMG Mori Lasertec 30 (40 micrometre layers, about 80 micrometres, 0.19 mm, 19/40/62 micrometres). Smallest features of the artefact: 0.8 mm pins and holes, 0.4 and 0.8 mm slots, 0.8 and 1.2 mm walls; it has no fillet or corner radius. Achieved tolerance grades IT10 for one machine and IT11 for the other, by X-ray computed tomography at about 35 micrometre voxels, with a measurement mean deviation of 14 micrometres and standard deviation of 11 micrometres per artefact. A beam offset adjustment of +0.05 mm with scaling brought the second machine to IT10. Ra falls from about 30 micrometres at 0 degrees to about 6 micrometres at 90 degrees on one machine. Described by its authors as preliminary results of a small round robin. Neither machine is the EOS M 290 30 micrometre card of this catalogue.
